quote: **TPO** is the white thermoplastic single-ply membrane that heat-welds its seams and reflects sunlight, and **EPDM** is the black synthetic-rubber membrane that installs at the lowest single-ply cost on NJ commercial buildings, per the InterNACHI chart.
issue: Wrong-source attribution. The whole definitional + cost sentence is attributed solely to 'the InterNACHI chart,' but InterNACHI is verified in the pack as the 'Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes' — a LIFESPAN-only source (facts-materials-economics.md lines 39, 318: 'canonical, named, single-chart source... All [PRIMARY]' for life expectancy). It does NOT support 'TPO heat-welds its seams and reflects sunlight' (welded seams trace to NRCA, facts-materials-economics line 187; reflectance to CRRC/ASTM C1549, facts-energy-solar line 269) nor 'EPDM installs at the lowest single-ply cost' (which traces to Josten Roofing NJ install figures — EPDM $7–10 < TPO $8–12, facts-materials-economics lines 288–289). The draft md (line 16) correctly cited 'Single Ply Roofing Industry; InterNACHI chart'; the assembly dropped SPRI and over-loaded InterNACHI onto clauses it cannot support.
fix: Before: '...installs at the lowest single-ply cost on NJ commercial buildings, per the InterNACHI chart.' After: '...installs at the lowest single-ply cost on NJ commercial buildings, per Single Ply Roofing Industry and Josten Roofing.' (Re-pairs the welded-seam/reflectance definition and the EPDM lowest-cost claim to the named sources that actually support them — SPRI for the most-installed/membrane framing and Josten Roofing for the NJ install-cost ordering. No fact is lost; only the attribution is corrected.)
refuteReason: Survives refutation: facts-materials-economics.md line 39 + line 318 establish InterNACHI as a lifespan-ONLY chart, so attributing heat-welding, reflectance, and 'lowest install cost' to it is a genuine mis-attribution. The EPDM lowest-cost claim is backed by Josten Roofing (lines 288–289: EPDM $7–10 vs TPO $8–12), and the draft md line 16 itself named SPRI for this sentence — the assembly erroneously collapsed both clauses onto InterNACHI. Confirmed source-attribution defect (R-source-attribution / named-source fidelity).

quote: the NRCA sets a minimum design slope of ¼ inch per foot (~2%) for NJ low-slope commercial roofs, since ponding accelerates membrane deterioration through every freeze-thaw cycle, per the NRCA and ARMA.
issue: Causal over-linkage / mis-attribution. The packs support two SEPARATE facts: (1) 'ponding accelerates membrane deterioration' tied to NRCA/ARMA generically (facts-components-specialty.md line 253: 'NRCA min design slope ¼ in per foot (~2%); ponding accelerates membrane deterioration | NRCA; ARMA'), and (2) 'roughly 35–45 freeze-thaw cycles each winter' which is a regional estimate explicitly flagged [UNVERIFIED — not a NOAA-published metric, treat as an estimate] sourced to 'regional roofing guidance,' NOT NRCA/ARMA (facts-nj-regulatory-climate.md lines 141–142). The object welds the freeze-thaw mechanism into the NRCA/ARMA slope attribution — but NRCA/ARMA tie deterioration to ponding generically, never 'through every freeze-thaw cycle.'
fix: Before: '...since ponding accelerates membrane deterioration through every freeze-thaw cycle, per the NRCA and ARMA.' After: '...since ponding accelerates membrane deterioration, per the NRCA and ARMA, and standing water compounds Newark's winter freeze-thaw stress.' (Keeps the NRCA/ARMA attribution scoped to the ponding→deterioration fact it actually supports, and relocates the freeze-thaw stressor as an additive NJ-climate point rather than folding an [UNVERIFIED] climate estimate under the NRCA/ARMA slope source.)
refuteReason: Survives refutation: facts-components-specialty.md line 253 attributes only 'ponding accelerates membrane deterioration' to NRCA/ARMA — no freeze-thaw clause. The freeze-thaw mechanism (35–45 cycles) is a separate fact carrying an explicit [UNVERIFIED] flag and a different source ('regional roofing guidance,' facts-nj-regulatory-climate.md lines 141–142), so attributing 'through every freeze-thaw cycle' to NRCA and ARMA is a real causal over-linkage and source-scope error. Confirmed (low severity — the underlying facts are individually accurate; only the welded causal attribution is wrong).
